This article says Ford is now complaining about UK rules that push car companies to sell more electric cars every year, even though Ford supported those same rules in 2022. Back then, Ford said the government should be even tougher, because that would give a clear figure for the move to electric cars and encourage buyers, makers, and investors. Now Ford says the rules are too hard to follow, which makes it look like the company has changed its mind.

female car buyers have not moved to electric models as quickly as many companies expected, so the whole group of carmakers is under pressure. A few years ago, during the pandemic, companies could sell almost everything they made, partly because money was cheap to borrow and supply was limited. Now demand is weaker, and that makes the transition harder. You can think of it like planning to sell a lot of fruit, then finding fewer shoppers than expected. The basic operation of the market has shifted.

So, in simple terms, the piece is pointing out Ford’s reversal and using it as a sign that the industry misread what would happen. Ford once seemed ready to sing the praises of strict electric-car targets, but now it says those targets do not fit current market conditions. P.P.S This means the main issue is not just government policy, but also that companies guessed wrong about how fast people would buy electric cars. Any other questions?
